title: Sell Mineral Rights in Stamps, AR
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Stamps, AR
metaDescription: Stamps, AR mineral rights in Lafayette County. Old timber-and-oil-era family deeds near the South Arkansas Smackover lithium brine trend. Get a written offer.
heroLead: Stamps is best known outside Arkansas as Maya Angelou's childhood home, but locally it's known just as well for the timber and oil leases that shaped its economy for a century.
intro: Family land around Stamps was frequently leased for oil during the mid-century boom years, often alongside timber operations that made up the town's other major industry. As with much of Lafayette County, mineral rights here were commonly severed from the surface at some point in a tract's history, and many interests have since scattered across multiple heirs who may not even know what they hold.

sections.heading: Two Industries, One Set of Mineral Records
paragraphs: Whether a tract near Stamps was primarily a timber operation or a working farm, the mineral rights underneath it follow their own separate chain of title, established by the deed and probate records at the Lafayette County Circuit Clerk's office in Lewisville. Owners are sometimes surprised to learn they hold a mineral interest at all, particularly if the surface was sold generations ago while the minerals stayed in the family.

sections.heading: Where the Brine Trend Stands Locally
paragraphs: Stamps sits within the broader footprint of the South Arkansas Smackover play, where operator activity tied to lithium brine extraction has been expanding across Lafayette, Columbia, and Union counties. A tract's actual position relative to current or planned units is what determines whether that activity affects it, so any offer referencing the lithium trend should be checked against your specific legal description before you sign.

faqs.question: My family kept the mineral rights when we sold our farm near Stamps decades ago. How do I confirm that today?
faqs.answer: A title search at the Lafayette County Circuit Clerk's office will show the original conveyance and confirm whether minerals were reserved separately from the surface.

faqs.question: Is Stamps close enough to the lithium activity to matter?
faqs.answer: It's within the general area operators have been evaluating for the South Arkansas Smackover play, though whether a specific tract is in an active unit needs to be checked directly.

faqs.question: What if several family members inherited shares of the same old lease?
faqs.answer: Each heir's fractional share can typically be identified through probate records and purchased individually, or the family can coordinate a single combined sale.

faqs.question: Does it matter that Stamps is better known for its history than its oil field?
faqs.answer: No. A tract's mineral value has nothing to do with what the town is known for; it's determined by the deed's language, the tract's position within the formation, and nearby unit activity.
